data.title: S&P 500 posts weekly losses amid oil, rate concerns
data.description:
Wall Street rallied on Friday after the latest consumer inflation report came in broadly in line with expectations, helping ease concerns over price pressures and supporting a rebound across risk assets.

On Friday, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.9%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) advanced 0.86%, and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.9%. 

Despite Friday’s rebound, the S&P 500 slipped 0.8% for the week.

Seeking Alpha analyst Agar Capital noted, “The week was dominated by macroeconomic factors, particularly oil, which once again surpassed $100, and bond yields, which continued to be a nuisance. After three negative sessions, stock indices closed the week with a strange surge higher, despite the still-high inflation figure, which increased the probability of a rate hike at the September meeting from 60% to 90%. After the figure, yields first rose, then fell. Equities initially moved lower, then recovered and closed the day in the green. This was most likely because investors decided to look through the bad news already priced in, such as the September rate hike, while still discounting the possibility of a new round of Fed tightening.”

From a sector-level perspective, three S&P sectors ended the week in positive territory, while the remaining eight sectors finished in the red.

Energy (XLE) and Communication Services (XLC) were the strongest-performing sectors of the week, gaining 1.7% and 0.54%, respectively.

Seeking Alpha analyst Jack Bowman highlighted that it's no surprise to see energy up again this week after the recent gains in oil. The longer and messier the U.S.-Iran war gets, the more I expect we'll see energy gain, as their revenues will stay higher for longer. Megacap tech firms (GOOGL, MSFT, etc.) held their ground, which buoyed both tech and communications in a week where there was otherwise a lot of market pain.

Conversely, Health Care (XLV) and Materials (XLB) posted the weakest weekly performances, falling 3.52% and 2.84%, respectively.

Bowman concluded, “When defensive sectors like healthcare and cyclical sectors like industrials sell off together, it tends to tell me that we're looking at rate fears plaguing the market. When a macro thesis is driving, there isn't much room for traditional defense, and I expect that volatility to continue across both defensives and cyclicals until we get clarity on rates next week.”

data.title: L’Oréal faces Arizona suit over alleged hair relaxer cancer risks
data.description:
Arizona has filed a lawsuit against L’Oréal SA (LRLCF) and its US subsidiary, alleging the cosmetics company failed to disclose potential cancer risks associated with its hair-relaxer products.

Attorney General Kristin Mayes filed the case in state court Thursday, making Arizona the first state to pursue legal action over alleged cancer risks tied to hair relaxers. The state is seeking financial penalties and damages, along with an order requiring L’Oréal (LRLCF) to warn consumers about the alleged risks or stop selling the products.

The lawsuit focuses on hair relaxers sold under brands including Dark and Lovely and Optimum. The products, which permanently straighten textured hair, are used predominantly by African American women.

Arizona alleges that L’Oréal (LRLCF) and related companies marketed the products to women and children for decades while failing to adequately address potential health concerns.

The lawsuit adds to more than 12,000 similar cases filed by women and their families, which have been consolidated in federal court in Chicago.

The litigation gained momentum after a 2022 National Institutes of Health study reported that women who frequently used hair relaxers were more than twice as likely to develop uterine cancer.

L’Oréal (LRLCF) USA has rejected the allegations, saying its products are safe and that the claims lack scientific and legal merit.

data.title: Dell Technologies soars 12% to set new high
data.description:
Dell Technologies (DELL) shares jumped almost 12% on Friday, closing at $566.99, a gain of $60.37 on the session. The advance came as the technology infrastructure company extended a strong recovery following its record fiscal second-quarter earnings report on September 1. 

The earnings-driven rally that began on September 2, when shares surged nearly 16% on blowout results, has continued to find support as analysts and investors absorbed the scale of Dell's AI backlog and raised fiscal-year outlook.

data.title: Wall Street rallied after the latest inflation report came in largely in line
data.description:
Wall Street’s major averages closed higher on Friday after the latest consumer inflation report came in largely in line with expectations.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) finished +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) ended +0.8%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) closed +0.9%. 

From a sector-by-sector vantage point, nine of the 11 segments concluded in the green, with communication services leading the charge. At the other end of the spectrum, utilities were the weakest performer. 

U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in August, matching forecasts after a 0.1% gain in July and leaving the year-over-year rate unchanged at 3.4%. Core CPI (ex-food and energy) increased 0.3% versus the 0.2% consensus and prior reading, while the annual core rate eased to 2.4% from 2.5%, in line with estimates. 

“Friday's CPI print was in-line with expectations, but inflation is still too hot, and the Federal Reserve's hands are tied. A rate hike next week is all but assured. Consumer prices are going in the wrong direction, and remain significantly higher than the Fed's 2% target,” Skyler Weinand of Regan Capital stated. 

U.S. Treasury yields were mixed. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.63%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) ticked up by 1 basis point to 4.97%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) dipped 2 basis points to 5.35%. 

“For what it’s worth we at Cestrian believe that the ‘bonds are going to zero’ narrative is going to prove fatally incorrect and we are, in fact, bullish ZROZ and TLT with a 12 month timeframe in mind,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Dell Technologies (DELL) climbed higher by +11.9%, while shares of Albemarle Corporation (ALB) fell -3.5%

data.title: SA analyst: Lower yields could ignite stocks and crypto
data.description:
Wall Street rallied Friday after the latest consumer inflation report came in broadly in line with expectations, helping ease concerns over price pressures and supporting a rebound across risk assets.

Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research struck an optimistic tone on the outlook, despite a difficult week for traditional portfolios.

“This week, you were happy if you owned oil or Ether, strange bedfellows those, and unhappy if you owned stocks or bonds,” King stated.

On Friday the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) gained +0.9%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) advanced +0.8%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) climbed +0.9%. 

King said Cestrian rejects the increasingly bearish outlook for government bonds, arguing that the “bonds are going to zero” narrative is likely to prove wrong.

“We are, in fact, bullish ZROZ and TLT with a 12 month timeframe in mind,” he said, signaling confidence that longer-duration Treasury ETFs could benefit over the coming year.

King also maintained a constructive view on equities and cryptocurrencies, despite recent market volatility. 

“We also believe equities and crypto are going to close the year higher than here,” King said.

data.title: Element Solutions reinstated Buy at Goldman as focus shifts back to standalone execution
data.description:
Element Solutions (ESI) shares wobble between small gains and losses in Friday's trading as Goldman Sachs reinstated coverage with a Buy rating and $44 price target as the focus shifts back to standalone execution following the termination of the Solstice merger.

Goldman analysts led by Duffy Fischer said the merger termination is a positive catalyst because it "removes risk, prevents dilution, and allows ESI management to focus on high-return organic projects."

Element Solutions (ESI) experiences robust underlying demand driven by AI infrastructure and data center buildouts, high-margin growth, which is a primary growth engine for the company, and the analysts think the company's asset-light model allows it to capture high-margin AI growth faster than peers.

The company continues to reshape its earnings mix through strategic transactions, including the divestiture of its graphics business and bolt-on acquisitions such as EFC and Micromax, and Goldman says the management team has proven adept at adding value through focused M&A and expects more deals to come in over the next several years.

Element Solutions (ESI) shares are down ~10% since the deal was announced, which the analysts believe provides an attractive entry point, as the company now trades at a significant valuation discount to peers that should shrink over time.

data.title: Roblox rolls out a wave of new features at RDC 2026
data.description:
Roblox (RBLX) is using its 2026 Roblox Developers Conference to mark its 20th anniversary and present a strategy centered on "more play, more building, and more growth." RDC is the company’s annual, invite-only event for developers and other creators who make games and virtual items on Roblox. Importantly, the event is where Roblox (RBLX) typically announces new platform tools, game engine updates, discovery changes, and ways for creators to earn money.

The headliner on Friday was the Roblox Everywhere reveal, which will let creators distribute Roblox (RBLX) experiences as standalone apps on mobile, PC, and consoles while relying on the company's underlying technology and services. By the end of 2026, Roblox also plans to let users open games directly in Google Chrome from an experience’s details page, eliminating the need to install the Roblox app, with support for other browsers planned for later.

Roblox (RBLX) also said it is working on offline solo play, with an early-access version expected before a broader release targeted for mid-2027. New social features include a Friends chat tab that carries across games.

For game makers, the company previewed Build, a prompt-based, mobile-focused creation tool designed to make game development more accessible to people without prior Studio experience. Roblox (RBLX) said 9K games had been published through Build’s New Zealand alpha by September 1, and 71% of its creators had not previously used Roblox Studio. The alpha version is expanding to Serbia and Singapore.

The company also announced an upcoming Scene Generator functionality, which will allow creators to use a text prompt and reference image to produce an editable game scene. Other development updates aim to better support 2D, puzzle, turn-based, and asynchronous multiplayer games, including new camera, sprite, interface, and notification tools.

Roblox is revising discovery to better match games with age groups, promoting shorter experiences for younger players and more involved, repeat-play games for older users. It also expanded Moments, its short-form gameplay-video feed, and plans to add shopping features that let users buy virtual items or backgrounds featured in videos.

In terms of boosting creator income potential, Roblox (RBLX) introduced Wallet, a Creator Hub financial account for eligible U.S.-based independent creators age 18 and older. It will make cleared earnings available in real currency each business day, beginning later this year. A linked Roblox Card is planned for 2027. 

Roblox said creators have earned more than $5B through its Developer Exchange program since 2013, including about $1.7B in the past year.

Shares of Roblox (RBLX) moved up 1.5% in late Friday afternoon trading.

data.title: Paramount told to start settlement talks with state AGs in late October
data.description:
Paramount Skyance (PSKY) and a group of 12 state attorneys general who sued to block the entertainment company's planned $110 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) were told by a judge to find dates for settlement talks late next month. 

No specific dates have been set, but the magistrate judge suggested the parties find two consecutive days in late October for in-person settlement talks, according to a court filing on Friday. The talks will be overseen by Magistrate Judge Thomas Hixson.

The latest update comes after California's AG Rob Bonta late last month canceled a meeting with representatives of Paramount (PSKY) to start discussing a settlement of the state’s lawsuit seeking to block the mega media deal.

Last month Paramount (PSKY) CEO David Ellison threatened to relocate the movie studio out of California if he couldn't reach a settlement with California's AG. Paramount (PSKY) would move the studio to Tennessee, Texas, Georgia, or another identified state if he can't reach a deal with Bonta by Oct. 1.
